title: Expandable Rollforward Credits & Usage Ceiling Experiment for Multi-year Renewals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers report friction when committing to multi-year contract bands because of usage volatility and perceived wasted commit. Proposal: run an experiment that offers a structured 'rollforward credit' mechanism paired with a soft usage ceiling. Customers signing multi-year contracts receive a limited pool of rollforward credits (X% of annual commit) that can be applied to cover overage in year N+1, plus an optional soft ceiling that throttles discounting beyond a threshold. Goal: increase multi-year conversion velocity and retention while limiting downside to Redwood unit economics.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment definition documented in Confluence and approved by RevOps and Legal
A/B cohort implemented in billing flow and contract templates for 5 pilot accounts
Metric guardrails: forecasted gross margin impact < 3% for pilot cohort and no worse than baseline for P50 scenario
Primary outcome: +6% increase in attach rate to multi-year discounts within pilot group vs control over 90 days
Secondary outcome: net dollar retention >= baseline and churn rate not increased
Playbook for sales to offer rollforward credits with templated contract language and FAQ
experiment_design: Cohorts: 1) Control (standard multi-year discount offer), 2) Treatment A (rollforward credits = 10% of annual commit), 3) Treatment B (rollforward credits = 20% + soft usage ceiling)
Sample: target 30 enterprise accounts in pilot across mid-market and enterprise segments; randomization at account renewal moment
Timebox: 90 day experiment window with weekly checkpoints
Metrics: multi-year conversion rate, MRR retention at 90 days, NDR projection, realized overage credits used, realized discounted revenue, gross margin delta
Measurement approach: upstream tags in CRM + billing events; tie to usage telemetry to compute realized credit consumption; statistical significance threshold p<0.10 due to pilot size
Rollback criteria: sustained margin erosion > 4% over any 2-week window or legal/revenue recognition blockers
tradeoffs: Pros: improves sales flexibility and reduces churn risk from overcommitment; visible offering for procurement conversations
Cons: adds complexity to billing and revenue recognition; potential for gaming if rollforward pool too large
Operational: requires updates to invoicing pipeline and contract playbook; Sales enablement burden
Mitigation: conservative initial credit percentage, built-in ceiling, and audit logs; phased rollout to Pilot accounts only
